title: Final Python Challenge
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Final Python Challenge in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Break the problem down
items.text: Large programs are easier to build when the problem is divided into small, understandable parts.

items.heading: Functions for reusable logic
items.text: Functions group reusable operations and keep repeated logic in one place.

items.heading: Classes for related data
items.text: Classes can model objects that combine related data and behavior.

items.heading: Conditions for decisions
items.text: if, elif and else let a program choose actions based on conditions.

items.heading: Loops for repetition
items.text: for and while repeat work when a task needs to run multiple times.

items.heading: Dictionaries for key-value data
items.text: Dictionaries are useful when values need to be looked up by meaningful keys.

items.heading: Exceptions for runtime problems
items.text: try, except and related statements let programs handle expected runtime problems safely.

items.heading: Virtual environments for dependencies
items.text: Virtual environments isolate packages so projects can use different dependency sets safely.

items.heading: Parameterized SQL
items.text: Parameterized queries keep values separate from SQL code and reduce SQL injection risk.

items.heading: Automated tests
items.text: Tests check expected behavior and help catch regressions when code changes.

items.heading: Logging and debugging
items.text: Logging records runtime information, while debugging helps inspect and fix incorrect behavior.

items.heading: Generators for large sequences
items.text: Generators produce values lazily and can reduce memory use when a large sequence does not need to exist all at once.

items.heading: Clear structure
items.text: Small responsibilities, meaningful names and clear organization make Python programs easier to maintain.
